component.name: Type As You Speak
component.summary: Speak, and your words are typed into the focused window — 100% locally

description.p: Type As You Speak is dictation, not transcription: it is an input method, like a keyboard. Press your Dictation key, talk, and the words appear in whatever application has focus — as you speak. There is no recording to upload, no queue, and no waiting.

Everything runs on your machine. Speech is transcribed locally with faster-whisper (the fast CTranslate2 build of Whisper), so your voice and your text never leave your computer. After the first model download it works completely offline, and there is no account, no telemetry, and no server.
While the microphone is live your audio output is muted, so you don't hear yourself; it's restored the moment the session ends. Works on Wayland and X11.
The store build runs on the CPU — no GPU or NVIDIA driver needed. Power users who want GPU acceleration can instead install from the source repository with install.sh.

New app icon: a clean, simplified vector design in a soft pastel palette, crisp in every package. Also: an automated GitHub Actions release pipeline (sdist, wheel, and a .deb per tagged release) and a RELEASES.md checklist for cutting releases.

App identity (icon, .desktop, AppStream) and the first distribution-channel packaging: Flatpak/Flathub, a .deb builder, an AUR PKGBUILD, and a Fedora/Copr spec — all CPU builds. tays also now starts the ydotool daemon automatically if it isn't running.
Added the tays models listing and per-run tays start --model NAME. The default model is now small.en — a lighter, faster first run; bump to medium.en or larger for more accuracy.
Added tays keybind: copy-paste steps to bind a Dictation key for your desktop (auto-detects KDE, GNOME, Sway, Hyprland, XFCE).
X11 support: keystroke injection works on both Wayland and X11, and the clipboard fallback is chosen per session (wl-copy or xclip).
Fixed the hallucination filter to strip Whisper's stock "closing" phrases wherever they appear in a commit, not only at the tail.

First release: Mac-like, type-as-you-speak dictation for Linux — the words you say are typed into the focused window as you talk. GPU auto-detect with CPU fallback, config-driven, and an idempotent no-sudo installer.
